items.title: Explicit formal QED vertex/free-line convention
items.statement:
Adopt the following coefficient convention for finite formal QED bookkeeping in
the Minkowski, units, and Clifford conventions of
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. In particular,
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $h=-\eta$,
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=2h^{ab}I_4$, and
$\not p:=\gamma^a h_{ab}p^b$. The inverse-length mass is
$\mu=m_{\rm rest,SI}c/\hbar$ and a declared physical charge $q_{\rm SI}$ has
dimensionless value $q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$.

A **formal coefficient graph** here is a finite directed graph of interaction
vertices and internal lines with a momentum covector assigned to each line and
momentum conservation imposed at each vertex. It records a coefficient at a
fixed finite or formal order; it is not, by this definition, a convergent
amplitude or an operator on a continuum interacting Hilbert space. For a Dirac
species of dimensionless charge $g$, use $D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a$ and adopt the
vertex factor $ig\gamma^a$. For an electron, $g=-e_{\rm n}$, so the vertex is
$-ie_{\rm n}\gamma^a$.

For $\mu>0$ and off-shell momentum $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$, set
$$S_0(p)=\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}.$$
The adopted fermion-line coefficient is $iS_0(p)$. In Feynman gauge the
auxiliary covariant photon-line coefficient is
$$D^F_{ab}(k)=-\frac{i h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0} =\frac{i\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}.$$
The symbol $+i0$ denotes the selected Feynman boundary-value convention when a
distributional line is used; it does not define products of singular loop
distributions. The coefficient $D^F_{ab}$ is a calculational tensor factor,
not a declaration of four positive physical photon polarization states.

For the formal matrix realization, use the coefficientwise inverse specified
by the planned interface [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]: if $K_0$ is an invertible
finite matrix and $K(z)=K_0+zV$, the formal inverse is the power series in
$z$; no convergence in $z$ is claimed. The planned off-shell/tree identities
of [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]] fix the $h=-\eta$ slash and the nonzero-denominator
conditions. When a time-ordered free distribution is needed, use the actual
carrier $H_\mu$ of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]], for which
$(\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0$ and whose definition has no extra prefactor
$i$. The distributional use of that carrier is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]; the formal coefficient factors above are adopted
independently of that optional distributional identification.

items.title: Specified finite spatial compact U(1) gauge regulator
items.statement:
Adopt as one selected regulated physical model the finite oriented-graph data
of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]], with finite nonempty vertex and link
sets, compact $U(1)$ rotor variables on links, finite CAR matter at vertices,
fixed integer background $b_x\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$, and the displayed Gauss
operators. The mathematical definition specifies
$\mathcal H_{\rm kin}=L^2(\mathbb T^E)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_a(\mathbb C^{s|V|})$,
the integer-spectrum electric operators $E_e$, link unitaries $U_e$, and the
Hamiltonian $H=H_0+V_B+V_F$ on its stated maximal domain
$D(H_0)$. This physical adoption does not add an embedding of the graph into
space or alter the mathematical definition's operator domains.

For the physical-unit assignment, the link angles, $E_e$, $U_e$, and finite CAR
operators are dimensionless. Assign units joules to $\lambda_E$, every
$\lambda_p$, and every entry of $M_x$ and $T_e$ in the displayed Hamiltonian;
then $H$ has units joules and $tH/\hbar$ is dimensionless with $t$ in seconds
and $\hbar$ in joule-seconds, as in [[def-qft-framework-units]]. The graph is
finite regulator data, not a coordinate lattice with an assigned spacing.

The adopted reading is limited to a model whose mathematical data are actually
constructed, consistent with [[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]].
The CAR construction inside [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]] is
conditional on Countable Choice and its inspected draft Fock/CAR supplier
interfaces; this postulate does not confer proof acceptance on those carriers.
It adopts no experimental result, measurement probability, continuum
approximation, Lorentz-invariant continuum theory, or claim that the model
describes nature.

items.title: Actual interacting physical Gauss-sector dynamics
items.statement:
Assume the fixed finite-graph model adopted by
[[post-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-model]]: a finite nonempty oriented graph,
$s\ge1$ finite CAR modes per vertex, fixed backgrounds
$b_x\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$, link electric operators $E_e$, the joint Gauss
operators $G_x$, and $H=H_0+V_B+V_F$ on the exact maximal domain
$D(H_0)$ of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]]. Assume the Axiom of Choice
and a constant $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. Then the physical sector
$$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\bigcap_{x\in V}\ker G_x$$
is nonzero. The restriction $H_{\rm phys}:=H|_{D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}$
is self-adjoint, and
$$\mathcal U_{\rm phys}(t)=e^{-itH_{\rm phys}/\hbar},\qquad t\in\mathbb R,$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ with the
exact derivative domain $D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$. This is an exact
fixed-regulator result conditional on the stated mathematical suppliers; it
asserts no continuum dynamics or continuum QED construction.

items.title: Exact Ward/Gauss predictions in adopted regulator
items.statement:
Assume the finite-graph model of
[[post-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-model]] and the Axiom of Choice. Write
$\mathcal U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for the unitary group of
[[pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-existence]], and let
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\bigcap_x\ker G_x$ be its nonzero physical sector.

For a bounded operator $O$ on $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$, define its gauge charge
$q=(q_x)_{x\in V}\in\mathbb Z^V$ by
$$U(\alpha)OU(\alpha)^\dagger=e^{i\sum_x q_x\alpha_x}O \quad(\alpha\in\mathbb T^V).$$
For each normalized $\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$,
$\langle\psi,O\psi\rangle=0$ when $q\ne0$. A finite product of bounded
gauge-charge eigenoperators has zero expectation whenever the sum of its
charge vectors is nonzero. If $O$ maps $D(G_x)$ into itself and
$[G_x,O]$ extends to a bounded operator, then
$\langle\psi,[G_x,O]\psi\rangle=0$. These statements also hold for
$O(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger O\mathcal U(t)$; the finite-regulator evolution
preserves gauge charge and the domains $D(G_x)$.

For a fixed vertex $x$, distinct real insertion times $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ with
$n\ge1$, bounded operators $O_j$ that map $D(G_x)$ into itself, and bounded
commutators $[G_x,O_j]$, define ordinary time ordering by placing the factor
with larger time to the left. With
$O_j(t_j)=\mathcal U(t_j)^\dagger O_j\mathcal U(t_j)$ and
$G_x(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger G_x\mathcal U(t)$, the following identity holds
as a distribution in $t$ between normalized physical/domain vectors:
$$\frac{d}{dt}\left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left[G_x(t)\prod_{j=1}^nO_j(t_j)\right]\psi\right\rangle =\sum_{j=1}^n\delta(t-t_j) \left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left([G_x,O_j(t_j)]\prod_{i\ne j}O_i(t_i)\right)\psi\right\rangle.$$
The products are evaluated on the stated common domains and $G_x$ is
bosonic, so no grading sign is inserted.

For a region $R\subseteq V$, define its boundary links by
$$\partial R=\{e\in E:\text{exactly one endpoint of }e\text{ lies in }R\},$$
with $\epsilon(e,R)=1$ for a link directed out of $R$ and $-1$ for a link
directed into $R$. On
$\mathcal D_R=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}\cap\bigcap_{e\in\partial R}D(E_e)$, put
$Q_R^{\rm lat}=\sum_{x\in R}(n_x-b_xI)$. If bounded $O$ preserves
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, maps each boundary $D(E_e)$ into itself, and
$E_eO\phi=OE_e\phi$ for every $\phi\in D(E_e)$ and every $e\in\partial R$,
then $[Q_R^{\rm lat},O]\psi=0$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D_R$. Consequently,
an operator that changes $Q_R^{\rm lat}$ by a fixed nonzero charge cannot
satisfy all these preservation and boundary-commutation hypotheses while
acting nontrivially on that domain.

There is also a separate conditional continuum implication; it does not assert
that a continuum representation exists. Let $\mathcal H_c$ be a Hilbert space
and $D\subseteq\mathcal H_c$ a common invariant dense domain. For real
$f,g_k\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, let
$\rho(f),E_k(g_k):D\to D$ be linear assignments and put
$E(\mathbf g)=\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(g_k)$ for real
$\mathbf g=(g_1,g_2,g_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Fix
$\varepsilon_0>0$ and assume
$$\rho(f)=-\varepsilon_0\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(\partial_k f) \quad(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)).$$
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be compact. Suppose bounded $O$ maps $D$ into
itself and $E(\mathbf g)O\psi=OE(\mathbf g)\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$ whenever
$\operatorname{supp}\mathbf g$ is disjoint from $K$. For integers
$R\ge R_0$, suppose real $\chi_R\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ equals $1$ on a
neighborhood of $K$, $\operatorname{supp}\nabla\chi_R$ is disjoint from $K$,
and, with $Q_R^{\rm cont}:=\rho(\chi_R)
=-\varepsilon_0E(\nabla\chi_R)$, there is $Q:D\to D$ such that
$Q_R^{\rm cont}\psi\to Q\psi$ and
$Q_R^{\rm cont}O\psi\to QO\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$. Then
$[Q,O]\psi=0$ on $D$. If also $[Q,O]\psi=qO\psi$ on $D$ for a fixed
$q\ne0$, boundedness of $O$ implies $O=0$ on $\mathcal H_c$. This clause is
conditional on the displayed common-domain, Gauss, locality and limit
hypotheses only.

items.title: Qualified formal/tree gauge-current identities
items.statement:
Use the coefficient convention of [[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] and
formal ring of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Let $\zeta$ denote finite graph
link data, $z$ a formal indeterminate, and
$K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$
with $d\ge1$ and $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$. For each vertex-angle
tuple $\theta$, let $\zeta^\theta$ and the invertible diagonal matrix
$D_\theta$ be the finite gauge action and phase matrix of
[[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Assume the coefficient matrices
satisfy
$$K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}.$$
Let $S(z;\zeta)$ be the coefficientwise formal inverse specified by
[[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Then
$$S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad \det K(z;\zeta^\theta)=\det K(z;\zeta).$$
For a differentiable phase path $D_s=e^{is\Theta}$, assume also that
$K_0(\zeta^s)$ and $V(\zeta^s)$ vary differentiably along the gauge orbit
$\zeta^s$. Coefficientwise differentiation then gives
$$\delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S.$$
These are finite/formal identities only; the formal variable is not assigned
a numerical value and no convergence is asserted.

For the tree-current clause, take $\mu>0$ and four future-shell momenta
$p,p',q,q'$ with $h(p,p)=h(p',p')=h(q,q)=h(q',q')=\mu^2$, in inverse-length
units, and put $k=p-p'=q'-q$. Let
$$J_1^a=\bar u(p')\gamma^a u(p),\qquad J_2^b=\bar u(q')\gamma^b u(q),$$
where $\bar u=u^\dagger\beta$ and the spinors satisfy the corresponding
positive-energy Dirac equations
$(\not p-\mu)u(p)=0$, $(\not p'-\mu)u(p')=0$,
$(\not q-\mu)u(q)=0$, $(\not q'-\mu)u(q')=0$ and their Dirac-adjoint
left equations, in the $h=-\eta$ convention of
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. For a finite scalar $c(k)$, set
$\Delta D_{ab}(k)=c(k)k_a k_b$. Then
$$J_1^a\Delta D_{ab}(k)J_2^b=0.$$
For either displayed conserved current, the contraction with a covector
$\epsilon_a$ is unchanged by $\epsilon_a\mapsto\epsilon_a+\rho k_a$ for
finite $\rho\in\mathbb C$. If $c(k)$ is a rational coefficient containing
$1/h(k,k)$, require $h(k,k)\ne0$ at the selected momentum; a distributional
$+i0$ boundary value is not a pointwise finite $c(k)$. The adopted off-shell
fermion coefficient has denominator $h(p,p)-\mu^2$ and is used only when
that denominator is nonzero. No internal-line singular product is used here.
The tree clause is limited to these explicit finite contractions and does not
assert gauge independence for arbitrary diagrams.

items.title: Explicit soft-profile family has no strong Fock state limit
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], the positive transverse
free-photon model [[post-qft-free-photon-model]], and the exact conditional
mathematical interface stated below. Use the one-particle space
$\mathcal H_T=\{u\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3):
\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}$
of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ and
$\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$. Use the symmetric Fock sectors and
second-variable-linear pairing of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Define
$E(f)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}f^{\otimes n}/\sqrt{n!}$ and
$C(f)=e^{-\|f\|^2/2}E(f)$.

Fix a unit vector $\mathbf e\in\mathbb R^3$, a dimensionless
$\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and inverse-length cutoffs
$0<\epsilon<\kappa$. Put
$$f_\epsilon(\mathbf k)= \lambda\,\mathbf1_{\{\epsilon<|\mathbf k|<\kappa\}} |\mathbf k|^{-3/2}P_T(\mathbf k)\mathbf e.$$
Here $\mathbf k,\epsilon,\kappa$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$,
$\hbar c$ has units joule-metres, and $f_\epsilon$ has momentum-wavefunction
units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$. Let $d\Omega$ be standard surface area measure on
$S^2$. On sector $n$, let $N$ multiply by $n$ and let
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ act by the maximal multiplier
$\hbar c\sum_{j=1}^n|\mathbf k_j|$, with zero on the vacuum, as in the
planned free-photon model. With $C_\lambda=8\pi\lambda^2/3$, the conditional
coherent-family result gives
$$\langle C(f_\epsilon),NC(f_\epsilon)\rangle =C_\lambda\log(\kappa/\epsilon),\qquad \langle C(f_\epsilon),H_\gamma C(f_\epsilon)\rangle =\hbar c C_\lambda(\kappa-\epsilon).$$
Each $C(f_\epsilon)$ is a normalized vector in the number and energy
operator domains. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, this family has no norm limit,
even after arbitrary phase choices, and converges weakly to zero; zero is not
a normalized state. This exact free-model family does not construct an
interacting charged sector or scattering limit and reports no observation of
photon emission.

items.title: Charged regulator insertion requires boundary flux change
items.statement:
Consider the idealized attempt to insert a nonzero charge in a region $R$ of the
finite-graph model of [[pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-ward]]. Let
$\partial R=\{e\in E:e\text{ has exactly one endpoint in }R\}$, with
$\epsilon(e,R)=1$ for links directed out of $R$ and $-1$ for links directed
into $R$, and put
$$Q_R=\sum_{x\in R}(n_x-b_xI).$$
On
$$\mathcal D_R=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}\cap \bigcap_{e\in\partial R}D(E_e),$$
suppose a bounded operator $O$ preserves $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, maps each
boundary domain $D(E_e)$ into itself, and satisfies
$E_eO\phi=OE_e\phi$ for all $\phi\in D(E_e)$ and all
$e\in\partial R$. Then
$$[Q_R,O]\psi=0\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal D_R).$$
If, in addition, $[Q_R,O]\psi=qO\psi$ on $\mathcal D_R$ for a fixed
$q\ne0$, then $O\psi=0$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D_R$. Thus a
charge-changing insertion cannot act nontrivially on this domain while
preserving the physical sector and commuting with every boundary electric
operator. This is a fixed-regulator statement; it does not claim a continuum
charged-sector or general locality theorem.
